brique._comment: Engine-native Reflexive family capacity. kind/wrapper/rel_ctx/lang do not apply here.

objective.name: edit.patch_meaning
objective.description: Patch one or more local meaning descriptors by top-level section replacement or ordered semantic operations, including paths through arrays.

#root.role: Validate one edit batch, patch local meaning descriptors item by item, and return one aggregated per-item result payload.

items._comment: Required non-empty patch batch. Each item accepts patch/patch_json for top-level section replacement and semantic_patch for precise ordered edits. Canonical semantic_patch is { operations: [{ op: 'set'|'add'|'remove'|'delete'|'insert'|'test', path: (string|non-negative integer)[], value?: any }] }. Numeric segments address arrays; string segments, including '0', address object keys. delete omits value; every other op requires it. Legacy {add:[...], remove:[...]} remains accepted but cannot be mixed with operations. Example: {"semantic_patch":{"operations":[{"op":"set","path":["brique","engine_config","interfaces",0,"name"],"value":"llm_llm"}]}}.

result._comment: Per-item result list. Each item: { ok (bool), type (string), name (string) } on success, or { ok: false, ..., error: { code, message, reason } } on failure.

effects.meaning_descriptors: Meaning descriptor files under the current context may be rewritten.

transformation_contract.morphing: A batch of meaning patch requests becomes a per-item patch result set, with each successful item materializing a new local meaning descriptor state.
invariants: edit.patch_meaning is batch-oriented and returns one result entry per parsed item.
Only supported local edit types can be patched; matter and structure items are explicitly refused because they are owned by MatterLoop.
Each successful item replaces only the provided top-level sections and/or applies semantic_patch operations atomically before re-validating meaning invariants.
semantic_patch supports ordered set, add, remove, delete, insert, and test operations with object-key and array-index path segments.
A failed semantic operation leaves the descriptor unchanged, and concurrent edits of the same descriptor are serialized across the complete read-modify-write cycle.
Existing descriptor keys retain their source order, replaced sections retain their existing position, and newly introduced sections are appended.
patch_json is authoritative when supplied and preserves the order inside replacement sections.
success: On success, each result item reports ok=true with the normalized type and name of the patched element.
Mixed batches can succeed partially because invalid or refused items are returned as item-level errors in the same result array.
failure: The capacity fails when params.items is missing or cannot be parsed into a valid edit batch.
Individual items return errors when the target is unsupported, missing, outside scope, invalid JSON, fails invariants, or cannot be written atomically.
notes: Patch semantics remain section replacement semantics for patch/patch_json. semantic_patch.operations is the canonical precise mutation form; legacy add/remove remains compatible.
Structured patch objects remain supported for compatibility but cannot preserve caller key order after map decoding; use patch_json when replacement-section order matters.
Item-level errors are part of the normal payload contract for mixed edit batches.
